subject: System Design
title: Instagram's Image Pipeline
description: A micro-lesson that makes Instagram's Image Pipeline usable.

hook.text: Two billion users upload 100 million photos daily. Each photo needs 6 sizes. That's 600 million images per day.

buildup.text: Instagram stores original images in object storage and generates thumbnails asynchronously after upload.

discovery.text: A CDN serves images from the edge server nearest to the viewer, reducing latency from seconds to milliseconds.

twist.text: Storage costs grow forever. Stored photos never go away. Instagram uses tiered storage — hot, warm, cold.

climax.text: Instagram's image pipeline is a masterclass in async processing, CDN distribution, and tiered storage.

punchline.text: Upload once, resize async, serve from the edge.

quiz.question: Why does Instagram generate thumbnails asynchronously?
options: To avoid blocking the upload and making the user wait
